title: Sticky SNAT port reuse causing DNS response association across tenants after gateway failover
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported intermittent DNS answers that did not match expected records after a dedicated VPC gateway failover or during aggressive autoscaler scale-down events. Investigation shows ephemeral SNAT port reuse combined with stale conntrack entries on the egress gateway can cause DNS UDP responses to be delivered to the wrong tenant's socket namespace, exposing cross-tenant DNS responses. This ticket captures the root-cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and the planned long-term fix and rollout strategy.
reproduction_steps: Provision two tenants A and B sharing an egress gateway via peering and VPC NAT.
Generate high-volume short-lived UDP DNS queries from Tenant A to upstream resolver while autoscaler triggers scale-down on worker pods.
Trigger a failover of the egress gateway (simulate ctrl-plane promote or node reboot) to force conntrack table rebuild and SNAT port reallocation.
Observe that some DNS replies that should go to Tenant A are accepted by socket in Tenant B's network namespace when source IP:port collisions occur.
Reproducible at lower scale when conntrack timeouts + source port reuse align (race window ~5-12s observed in lab).
impact_summary: Customer-facing: incorrect DNS answers for a small fraction of requests leading to service errors or misrouting. Reported by three Dedicated customers in APAC/EMEA during peak churn.
Security: cross-tenant information leakage risk limited to DNS UDP payloads (no TCP state observed), rated high priority for enterprise customers.
Operational: incidents correlate with aggressive scale-down windows and gateway failovers; increases on-call load and SLA violation risk.
short_term_mitigation: Applied a hotfix to the gateway image that forces conntrack flush for tenant conntrack zone on egress gateway failover; rolled to one canary region (eu-west-1) during off-peak.
Added tighter SNAT ephemeral port allocation to prefer non-overlapping port ranges per-tenant to reduce collision probability.
Temporarily increased conntrack timeouts and added alerting for abnormal source-port reuse rates.
Customer communication: notified impacted tenants with mitigation steps and scheduled maintenance window for full roll-out.
root_cause_analysis: Egress gateway uses a shared NAT pool across tenant namespaces for SNAT. Under port pressure (many short UDP flows), the kernel reuses ephemeral ports quickly.

Conntrack entries survive gateway failover due to delayed cleanup in the connection-tracking subsystem; when ports are reused, replies are associated with stale conntrack tuples mapped to the wrong namespace socket.
VPC peering asymmetry and return-path rewriting caused response packets to traverse a different path where namespace isolation checks were insufficient.
The resolver replies are small UDP datagrams; our DNS proxy accepts by port+IP match without namespace UID validation.
decision_notes: Short-term: maintain conntrack flush on failover + per-tenant SNAT port windows to reduce blast radius (accepted).

Long-term: implement per-tenant conntrack zones at the kernel/iptables level and introduce deterministic source-port hashing keyed by tenant id to eliminate ambiguous reuse (design approved by infra lead).
Also require DNS proxy to verify the request origin (netns/uid) before delivering a response to an application socket; this adds a defensive check even with kernel fixes.

(ENG) Implement deterministic SNAT source-port allocator that seeds with tenant hash and epoch window (owner: Diego/Anika).
(ENG) Extend DNS proxy to include socket namespace validation on UDP replies (owner: Martin).
(SRE) Create canary rollout plan targeting eu-west-1 then us-east-1 with 1% -> 10% -> 100% steps and rollback criteria (owner: Priya).
(PM) Draft customer-facing postmortem and mitigation timeline for affected accounts (owner: Nora).
(SEC) Conduct threat review of cross-tenant leakage vector and sign off before global rollout (owner: Leo).
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy gateway image with conntrack-flush + port-window changes to eu-west-1 canary fleet (2/3 nodes) for 48 hours, monitor DNS error rate and conntrack churn.
Stage: if canary stable, expand to 10% of gateways and run for 24h with synthetic test harness simulating aggressive UDP churn.
Full: global rollout with per-tenant smoothing, schedule maintenance windows for large customers requiring reserved capacity; notify customers 72h in advance.
Rollback: if DNS mismatches >0.05% baseline or any cross-tenant complaint, revert gateway image and run emergency conntrack purge across impacted gateways.
